name: Net overseas migration, Australia (quarterly)
units: persons per quarter (net; can be negative)
notes: ABS 'National, state and territory population' components (Data API dataflow ERP_COMP_Q), Australia; dated the first day of the quarter; published in thousands to one decimal, converted to persons. known_after_days=275 from the quarter start: the quarterly release comes about 5.5-6 months after the quarter ends (e.g. December 2024 data in June 2025). Net overseas migration uses the '12/16-month rule', so preliminary quarters are model-based and are revised when final (about 18 months later); stored values are the latest revision. Category of travel changed in 2006 (12/16-month rule replaced the 12/12 rule). Negative in 2020-Q2 to 2021 (border closure), record +165,500 in 2023-Q1. Can be negative, hence diff.

Census R_DOMESTICMIG: V2010 evaluation estimates for 2001-2010, V2020 for 2011-2020, V2025 for 2021-2025 (method breaks at 2011 and 2021; county NIM is an allocation of the national total, not a count; it includes Armed Forces moves abroad in 2001-2010 and ICE detainees). Census PEP. known_after_days=310 is the largest first-release lag across vintages (county files normally mid/late March of t+1, about 255-270 days after July 1; V2018 came 2019-04-18 (291 d), V2020 2021-05-04 (307 d)). Stored values are the latest revisions (intercensal for 2000-2019 levels; final postcensal vintages for components), not the first release, so every year carries revision look-ahead. ANNUAL: about 25 observations; flagged, nearly untestable at daily move lengths.

name: Migrants arriving in the UK by small boat across the English Channel (daily)
notes: Home Office time series (SB_01) from the file dated 16 October 2026; every calendar day 2018-01-01 to 2026-10-15, explicit zeros on 2127 of 3210 days (no crossings, usually bad weather). Provisional operational data, revised (9 days flagged 'Revised'); the quarterly 'Illegal entry routes' release is authoritative. known_after_days=7: the full series is refreshed weekly on Fridays through the previous day; since 2022 a 'last 7 days' page is updated daily (next-day figures), but 2018-2021 values were compiled later, so 7 is the conservative bound. Transform level (daily event counts) rather than anomaly_log1p: zero-heavy, weather-driven and seasonal (summer-autumn peaks), but the series starts in 2018, so the 3-year anomaly warm-up would leave it out of every test period. Only the 2020-2025 period can include it.

name: US refugee admissions (arrivals) per month
source: US State Department, Refugee Processing Center (WRAPS)
notes: Refugee Admissions Report as of 30 September 2026 (one sheet per fiscal year FY2001-FY2026), 'Grand Totals' row by month; every fiscal year's months sum to its FY total, and FY2012-2017 and FY2019-2020 match the archived 'Arrivals by Region by Month' files exactly (check_refugee_archives.py). Dated the 1st of the calendar month. Excludes SIV recipients. Policy-driven: post-9/11 halt (Oct-Nov 2001: 4 a month), FY2018-21 ceilings cut, COVID pause (Apr 2020: 27), the January 2025 suspension (Feb-Sep 2025 under 200 a month), FY2026 almost all South Africans. 2 zero months. Seasonal (end-of-fiscal-year push in August-September; calendar months explain 26% of monthly log changes), hence anomaly_log1p (zero-safe). known_after_days=60 from the 1st: the report is normally updated early the next month (the 30 Sep 2026 edition was posted 2026-10-05); 60 allows for delays such as the Oct-Nov 2025 shutdown (the FY2025 year-end archive file is dated 2025-11-21).
